conventions: Compound preposition renderings in this chapter: the ASV's *over against* is one rendering no morpheme owns a part of, so `al-penei` (34.1) fuses under rule 30 with the verbless clause's copula joining the whole expression, headed on the construct noun and on *over*, and the single-morpheme `mul` (34.6) takes the same compound whole. `al-pi` (34.5) is split instead, because the ASV spends *according to* on the preposition and *the word* on the construct noun, so each morpheme has a rendering of its own; the head of the preposition's unit is *according*, not the connective *to*. Read which of the two shapes the ASV wrote before reaching for either outcome.

The age idiom `ben` + numeral + `shanah` (34.7, *Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died*) is divided with the construct `ben` taking both the construction-supplied copula and *old*, discontinuous around the numeral phrase (rules 20, 25), while each numeral keeps its own English, the *a* of *a hundred* belongs to the numeral rather than to the plural counted noun, and `shanah` keeps *years*. Neither *old* nor the copula is `added`, and neither belongs to `shanah`.
report: Read all 12 verses end to end against the candidate table. No construction is analysed two ways without something in the source licensing the difference, so patches is empty.

Compound prepositions were the one real candidate. `al-penei` (34.1) fuses as *over against* under rule 30, while `al-pi` (34.5) splits into *according to* on the preposition and *the word* on the construct noun: in 34.5 each morpheme has a rendering of its own, in 34.1 neither owns a part of the compound. `mul` (34.6) is a single morpheme taking the same compound. Both *over against* units head on *over* (rule 24), and 34.1 heads its source on the construct (rule 23). Licensed, not a split.

Article counting is uniform: fronting onto the rectum's article where the rectum is rendered anarthrously (34.1 *the top of Pisgah*, 34.3 *the city of palm trees*); first article takes the phrase's single *the* in attributive phrases (34.2, 34.12); the demonstrative pronoun takes the one determiner with both articles unrepresented (34.6 *this day*); and a supplied *the* goes on the construct only where no article morpheme stands in the chain (34.1, 34.2, 34.5, 34.6, 34.8, 34.9, 34.11, 34.12). The two Td->Np treatments the table flags in 34.1 are that count run correctly: the article on Gilead gets nothing because the phrase's single *the* stands before the article of `ha-arets`.

The relative-plus-suffix pair is settled by reference, not by preference: 34.10 fuses `asher ... o` as *whom* because the suffix resumes the antecedent, while 34.11's suffix denotes Moses rather than the plural antecedent and so takes its own *him* (rule 22's closing paragraph). Both `arvot moav` phrases (34.1, 34.8) take a supplied *the* on the construct, and both appositional nominals carrying no preposition (34.1 *to the top*, 34.3 *of the valley*) take the supplied word under rule 33, whose own *to your mountain* example covers the directional case.

Object markers: two take the preposition through which the English verb reaches its object (*knoweth of* 34.6, *wept for* 34.8), the rest are unrepresented because the ASV writes those objects bare. The chapter's single `added` unit, the supplied *it* of *caused thee to see it* (34.4), is correct under rule 44 since the verb's one suffix is spent on *thee*. I checked every other supplied English word (copulas, presentative *there*, indefinite articles, subject pronouns, supplied *the*s) for the failure the lemma table is blind to, and found none folded into a morpheme that does not license it.

BSB: no genuine error. All three disagreement families are documented convention differences - six Td (BSB attaches every article to its noun, against rules 29/41/47), the `le` of `lemor` (rule 27), and the `et` of 34.6, whose pronoun the suffix carries (rule 16).

Two conventions recorded. No promotions: the chapter's non-obvious calls are all applications of rules already in the contract, and the one shape that might generalise - a relative fused with a resumptive verbal object suffix as *whom* - has no corpus counts in this briefing to carry it, so promoting it would rest on a single unit.
